primary.thesis: Laso Finance is a small, niche crypto project (as far as I can tell it works on crypto payments / prepaid-card style products for users and AI agents) and has no visible large-VC valuation anchor. There are two ways every high rung resolves NO. (a) The team may never ship a publicly tradable token before Jan 1, 2028. That alone resolves every rung NO. (b) If they do launch, it will most likely be a small community or fair launch, or a launchpad-style launch (for example on Base), with an FDV in the low single-digit to low double-digit millions one day after launch. Also, small-cap launches usually sell off during the first 24 hours as airdrop and early holders exit, so the 4pm ET next-day snapshot tends to land below the first-hour peak. I'd concentrate on NO at the top of the ladder, where both routes to NO overlap and where only a breakout launch pays YES.

basket.reason: A $50M FDV at day one would need a top-tier launch (a major exchange listing, heavy VC backing or a hot narrative). That is unlikely for a project this size, and a non-launch also pays.
$30M is still well above the typical day-one FDV of small payments or agent-finance tokens after the first-day sell-off. It also pays if no token launches.
$20M needs sustained demand through the next-day 4pm ET snapshot. Small launches usually lose value from their open, so the snapshot tends to be below the peak.
$15M is the lowest rung where I still think the no-launch scenario plus a modest launch scenario together clearly dominate. Lower rungs are closer to the likely range of a real launch.

failure_narrative: The basket loses if Laso launches a token before 2028 and it holds more than $15M (and above that, $20M, $30M or $50M) FDV at 4pm ET the next day. The most plausible path is a strong narrative tailwind. AI-agent payments or stablecoin-rails tokens (x402-style agent commerce, Base ecosystem launches) become a hot sector, and Laso launches into that mania through a Coinbase/Base-promoted venue, a big launchpad or a tier-1 CEX listing. A low-float, high-FDV structure would also help, because a small circulating supply bid up by retail multiplies into a large fully diluted number even on thin volume. A general crypto bull phase with alt-season risk appetite would make all of this more likely.
hedge_thesis: The primary fails in worlds where speculative appetite for small new crypto tokens is high at Laso's launch date. The mechanism: new-token FDVs are mostly set by marginal retail and degen capital chasing narratives. That capital is plentiful when BTC and ETH are rising, Base/Solana on-chain activity and launchpad volumes are elevated, and AI-agent / agentic-payments tokens (the Virtuals ecosystem, x402-related tokens) are rallying. So a hedge is a long position on the broader risk-on crypto state, meaning higher BTC/ETH prices, strength in the Base-ecosystem and AI-agent token sectors, and high Coinbase trading activity. Those are the same conditions that let a small payments project print a $15M+ FDV one day after launch.
